accounts.pressureForecastLogic: The supply pool covers every dispatchable account regardless of upstream type (OAuth + Responses API), filtered only by disabled / unauthorized / currently rate-limited. Burn forecasting still requires a quota window, so Responses API accounts and 5h-on-non-premium plans contribute capacity but skip burn projections. For each burn-eligible account we linearly extrapolate quota exhaustion from the current window usage ratio; accounts with elapsed < 5% of the window are excluded from ranking to avoid noise. Concurrency slot throughput is adaptive: 60s / avg_duration_ms (falls back to 6 rpm/slot, clamped to 1-30). Bulk-limit threshold is dispatchable − ceil(currentRpm / (avgConcurrency × rpm/slot)) — the minimum accounts required to absorb current RPM; falls back to 30% of samples when RPM = 0. Pool capacity is min(global RPM, dispatchable total concurrency × rpm/slot); event stream models both −1 exhaustion and +1 replenishment when accounts reset. RPM / future capacity ≥ 90% is high pressure, ≥ 100% is supply shortfall; the "soon" warning window is 20% of the active window (5h → 1h, 7d → 34h). The 429 signal is the fraction of dispatchable accounts that hit a 429 in the last hour, saturated at 30%. Acceleration factor = dominant + 0.5 × secondary (avoids double-counting correlated RPM/active signals), capped at ×2.5. If known samples cover < 40% we flag low confidence and avoid escalating risk from burn projections alone.

usage.tableFirstTokenHint: First Token = time from request start until the upstream emits the first real content token (text / reasoning / tool arguments). Reasoning models think before that point, so a first-token time close to the total duration is normal and does not mean the proxy got slower. If 'First Token Excludes Conn Acquire' is enabled in system settings, this column already excludes the WS connection acquire time (see the Conn Acquire column).
usage.tableTokensPerSecHint: Output throughput = output tokens ÷ generation seconds. When first-token time is present it is excluded (closer to pure decode speed); otherwise full duration is used. Failed or empty-output requests show -.
usage.tableTimingHint: First (blue pill) = time to the first real content token; Total (violet pill) = end-to-end duration. Value color: green good / amber slow / red very slow (each metric judged independently). Reasoning models often have first-token close to total duration.

promptFilter.title: Prompt Filter
promptFilter.description: Manage local prompt risk rules and review upstream cyber_policy hits.

risk.title: Request and identity risk profiles
risk.description: Aggregates local decisions and upstream CY evidence separately for trusted users, sessions, API keys, client networks, and upstream accounts.
risk.guardrail: Historical profiles provide operational recommendations only and never turn a currently safe request into a block by themselves.
risk.lockedProfilesHint: Shows only live conversation locks and user cooldowns, newest lock first.
risk.peopleProfilesHint: Shows identities traceable to a signed NewAPI user ID by default.
risk.nonPersonHint: Sessions, keys, networks, and upstream accounts are environment subjects used for tracing; they are not people.

conversationLock.title: CYB conversation lock
conversationLock.description: This session received an explicit upstream cyber_policy response. Rejected requests after the lock do not add strikes; an administrator may unlock it after confirming a false positive.
conversationLock.localDescription: This session was locked by a high-confidence local terminal rule, not by upstream CYB. Review the original request and model-review result through the audit reference before unlocking.
conversationLock.confirm: Unlock this conversation? Its original context remains present, so do this only after confirming a false positive.
conversationLock.conversationUnlockReason: Conversation manually unlocked after administrator review
conversationLock.userCooldownDescription: This verified user recently received an upstream CYB response. All sessions are rejected locally without adding duplicate penalties; releasing the cooldown clears every currently active CY lock for this user.
conversationLock.confirmUserCooldown: Release this user's safety cooldown? This also clears every currently active CY conversation lock for the user. Do this only after confirming a false positive or completing manual review.
conversationLock.userCooldownUnlocked: User safety cooldown released; {{count}} active locks cleared
conversationLock.userCooldownUnlockReason: User safety cooldown released after administrator review

trust.title: Temporary adaptive trust
trust.description: Skips synchronous DS review only for requests that local rules consider clean. Local high-risk rules, periodic profiles, and CY feedback remain active. Thresholds, expiry, or a new CY event restore synchronous review.
trust.revoked: Temporary trust revoked; synchronous model review restored
trust.basisDescription: Explains why this user is or is not in reduced model review, including sampling and the deadline for restoring a full review.
trust.basisFallbackReason: The system continuously evaluates clean reviews, observation time, current risk, and periodic sampling.
trust.personOnly: Only signed person profiles can receive temporary trust.
trust.dialogDescription: This is not a permanent allowlist. Profiles continue and rising risk revokes the exemption automatically.
trust.reasonHint: Required for auditing who reduced first-token latency, why, and for how long.
trust.safetyHint: Local high-risk rules still run. Only clean requests skip synchronous DS. The exemption ends on threshold breach, local high-risk decisions, or upstream CY.

promptFilter.loadingDesc: Syncing rule settings and hit logs.
promptFilter.saveQuarantined: Settings saved; {{count}} unsafe custom rule(s) were disabled
promptFilter.saveRefreshFailed: Settings were saved, but rules or logs could not be refreshed. Refresh the page later to retry.
promptFilter.ruleSaveConflict: Custom rules changed elsewhere. The latest version has been loaded; edit again before saving.
promptFilter.ruleSaveConflictRefreshFailed: Custom rules changed elsewhere, but the latest version could not be loaded. Refresh the page manually
promptFilter.ruleEditTargetMissing: The original rule was deleted or changed. Close this dialog and select it again.
promptFilter.advancedConfigInvalidTitle: Advanced protection configuration cannot be parsed
promptFilter.advancedConfigInvalidDescription: The original configuration has been preserved and will not be replaced with defaults. Fix the JSON or refresh the page before saving.
promptFilter.advancedConfigInvalidSave: Saving is blocked because the advanced protection configuration is invalid
promptFilter.coverageEveryRequest: Every extractable request enters the local protection pipeline
promptFilter.protectionSummaryDesc: Daily operations only need the enforcement and model-review policies. Compatibility and experimental controls stay collapsed until needed.

adaptiveReview.title: Adaptive model review
adaptiveReview.description: New identities receive full review. Signed people with sustained low risk automatically reduce synchronous model calls. Local rules and session correlation always run; a hit, CY, or rising risk restores full review immediately.
adaptiveReview.defaults: Current policy: {{minClean}} clean reviews across {{hours}} hours, {{sample}}% sampling, and at least one forced model review every {{forceHours}} hours.

promptFilter.recommendedApplied: Recommended protection values are ready; review and save them
promptFilter.recommendedAppliedWithStrength: Applied the “{{strength}}” recommended preset. Review and save.
promptFilter.simpleConfigHint: The overview keeps only the master switch and mode. Thresholds, layers, prompts, and payloads are consolidated under Advanced settings.
promptFilter.advancedDescription: The default view shows daily policies only. Model connectivity, request templates, and runtime compatibility controls expand on demand while preserving the existing configuration version.
promptFilter.dailyPolicyDesc: Two combined policies replace the scattered enable, mode, and failure-handling switches.
promptFilter.reviewTemplatesDesc: Optional request templates for the external review provider. Leave blank to use the server defaults.
promptFilter.newapiAdapterDesc: Configure only when signed policy events must be forwarded to a NewAPI deployment for identity-aware enforcement. It is not required for local filtering or external review.
promptFilter.expertSettingsDesc: Thresholds, GuardPipeline sources, decoding compatibility, and optional extensions.
promptFilter.expertSettingsWarning: These parameters are still consumed at runtime. Change them only for protocol compatibility, resource limits, or experimental capabilities.
promptFilter.testResultPipelineHint: The text is evaluated as one current-user prompt through the real GuardPipeline source classification, model-family profile, and final policy path. It does not make a generation request or persist local penalty state. Configured secondary review and sidecar checks still make external detector calls and may consume their service quota.
promptFilter.testResultLegacyFallbackHint: The server did not return a GuardPipeline decision, so only the legacy rule result is available. Verify that frontend and backend versions match.
promptFilter.strictTerminalHint: When enabled, a current-user Prompt enters terminal handling only when a strict:true rule remains above the block threshold after intent and context checks. Audit-only terms and dual-use tool names do not become terminal by themselves. Balanced profiles may still use secondary review; strict profiles skip downgrade.
promptFilter.advancedConfigPlaceholder: Configure normalization, cumulative risk, local sidecar, and output scanning. All are disabled by default.
promptFilter.advancedConfigHint: Each advanced layer has its own enabled switch. The server validates JSON before saving.

guard.title: Unified GuardPipeline
guard.simplifiedSummary: Current-user input is enforced synchronously; history, tools, and attachments remain shadow-audited by default.
guard.description: Use one source-aware review path for Responses, Chat Completions, Messages, and WebSocket traffic. The page exposes only policy choices that change review scope or outcomes; runtime budgets, caches, and queues are system-managed.
guard.globalModeHint: Controls the new GuardPipeline as a whole. Inherit keeps the existing prompt-filter switches, thresholds, and terminal-rule behavior unchanged.
guard.defaultProfileHint: Fallback review strength for providers without an explicit profile and for future or unknown model families.
guard.trustedOverridesHint: Accept profile or mode overrides only after NewAPI HMAC verification. When off, all review-profile and mode request headers are ignored so clients cannot lower enforcement.
guard.compatibilityHint: The default is Inherit. Disabling or tuning the new pipeline does not remove existing rules, sensitive words, secondary review, or cumulative-risk settings.
guard.providerDescription: Providers inherit the default profile unless you explicitly assign a different profile to GPT, Claude Code, Grok, or another model family.
guard.profileDescription: Profiles change inspection depth; a single security-related noun never becomes a terminal violation by itself.
guard.layersDescription: The current user prompt is synchronous enforcement and penalty evidence. Auxiliary sources default to Shadow audit. The only exception is a high-confidence composite operational instruction in one tool-output segment: it may warn or block the current request according to the global mode, but never counts as terminal, strike, or ban evidence.

performance.title: Guard Performance and First-token Latency
performance.description: Reuse exact segment decisions and optionally move shadow-only auxiliary scans off the client wait path, reducing repeated work without weakening enforcement-layer inspection.
performance.syncSafetyNotice: current_user, application_candidate, and every Warn or Enforce layer always finish synchronously. These settings can never bypass inspection of the current user prompt.
performance.budgetDescription: Current-user input and auxiliary sources such as history, tools, and attachments use independent total budgets. The recommended values balance inspection depth, first-token latency, and memory stability.
performance.maxCurrentUserBytesHint: Shared UTF-8 byte budget for current-user-controlled text in one request, from 8192 to 1048576. Recommended: 131072.
performance.maxAuxiliaryBytesHint: Shared UTF-8 byte budget for history, system context, tool output, attachments, and session context, from 0 to 262144. Recommended: 32768; 0 disables auxiliary scanning.
performance.scanChunkBytesHint: Target chunk size for bounded scan work, from 1024 to 65536. Recommended: 8192; it cannot exceed the current-user budget.
performance.scanOverlapBytesHint: UTF-8-safe overlap retained between adjacent scan chunks, from 64 to 8192. Recommended: 512; it must be smaller than the chunk size.
performance.maxSegmentsHint: Maximum text segments retained for one logical request, from 1 to 256. Recommended: 64; current-user segments take priority over auxiliary segments.
performance.overBudgetNotice: Exceeding a budget is recorded as truncation and handled by bounded audit. Length alone never blocks, penalizes, or bans a user.
performance.scanChunkBudgetError: Chunk size cannot exceed the current-user synchronous scan limit.
performance.scanOverlapChunkError: Overlap must be smaller than the chunk size.
performance.asyncShadowAuxiliaryHint: Queues ordinary Shadow auxiliary content. A high-confidence composite operational instruction in one tool-output segment is always confirmed synchronously and may warn or block according to the global mode. When disabled, ordinary shadow layers also remain synchronous. Existing configurations default to disabled.
performance.exactSegmentCacheHint: Reuses a decision only when the complete rule configuration and segment digest match exactly. It never performs fuzzy matching or changes scores and block decisions.
performance.cacheEntriesHint: Maximum exact segment decisions retained in memory, from 1 to 32768. Least-recently-used entries are evicted first.
performance.cacheTTLHint: Maximum reuse time for an exact segment decision, from 1 to 86400 seconds. Rule changes automatically use a different cache key.
performance.shadowWorkersHint: Workers that process Shadow-only auxiliary segments in the background, from 1 to 16. Start with 2 and observe CPU usage.
performance.shadowQueueHint: Maximum queued Shadow-only auxiliary jobs, from 1 to 4096. The default overflow policy never pushes scanning back onto the request goroutine.
performance.shadowOverflowModeHint: When the queue is full, skip this Shadow-only auxiliary audit and increment the dropped counter without moving scanning onto the request thread. Current-user warning and enforcement layers are unaffected.

inherit.label: Inherit Existing
inherit.description: Keep the current prompt-filter switch, mode, thresholds, and rules without introducing new enforcement behavior.

off.label: Off
off.description: Disable this GuardPipeline scope while the existing legacy filter continues to follow its current configuration.

shadow.label: Shadow
shadow.description: Inspect and record decision differences without blocking, warning, or accumulating penalties.

warn.label: Warn
warn.description: Record and return a warning without adding strikes or applying account/IP penalties.

enforce.label: Enforce
enforce.description: Apply allow, review, and block decisions; only confirmed violations may emit penalty events.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Default production profile focused on low false positives: block clear harmful intent and review ambiguity.

strict.label: Strict
strict.description: Uses deeper correlation and denser auditing, while terminal blocks still require high-confidence evidence.

research.label: Research
research.description: Allows defensive and dual-use analysis; explicit malicious execution, theft, or evasion remains blocked.

openai.label: OpenAI / Codex
openai.description: For GPT models, Codex CLI, and OpenAI-compatible Responses or Chat traffic.

anthropic.label: Anthropic / Claude Code
anthropic.description: For Claude models, Claude Code, and the Anthropic Messages protocol.

xai.label: xAI / Grok
xai.description: For Grok and xAI models connected through OpenAI-compatible protocols.

unknown.label: Unknown / Other
unknown.description: Used when a provider cannot be identified or a future model family is added, avoiding an unassigned policy.

current_user.label: Current User Prompt
current_user.description: Content explicitly submitted by the user in the current request; the primary source for review and penalty evidence.

history.label: Linked History
history.description: Inspect prior user content only when continuation, alias references, or split instructions clearly connect it.

system.label: System Context
system.description: System-role text is normally application-owned; use Shadow before Enforce to measure false positives.

developer.label: Developer Context
developer.description: Developer-role content normally belongs to application policy and should not be attributed to the end user by default.

instructions.label: Responses Instructions
instructions.description: Inspect top-level /v1/responses instructions to detect client-controlled changes and baseline differences.

tool_output.label: Tool Output
tool_output.description: Treat tool-returned content as untrusted data. A high-confidence composite operational instruction may block the current request, but never becomes terminal, strike, or ban evidence.

tool_arguments.label: Tool Arguments
tool_arguments.description: Inspect structured parameters and targets before file, network, shell, or other tools execute.

attachment_refs.label: Attachment References
attachment_refs.description: Inspect attachment, file_id, URL, and reference metadata; a separate extraction service can be connected later.

session_context.label: Correlated Session Context
session_context.description: Inspect earlier fragments only when trusted identity links the session and the current request explicitly asks to continue; Shadow is the safe default.

attachment_content.label: Extracted Attachment Content
attachment_content.description: Inspect text returned by the attachment extractor in Shadow mode by default, so quoted document content is not automatically attributed to the user.

promptFilter.normalizationSimplifiedDesc: Uses safe defaults for common encoding bypasses.

contextDiscount.title: Legitimate-context Discount
contextDiscount.simplifiedDesc: Recognizes defensive, educational, and operational context to reduce false blocks.
contextDiscount.description: Reduce dual-use false positives for auditing, remediation, and teaching, while preventing generic disclaimers from erasing explicit operational intent.
contextDiscount.enabledHint: When disabled, every rule keeps its raw enforcement score, increasing false positives for security research and log analysis.
contextDiscount.intentAwareHint: Classify operational attack actions before deciding how much discount is allowed. Keep this enabled for the recommended behavior.
contextDiscount.maxDiscountHint: Maximum score reduction for defensive, remediation, or explanatory contexts. Higher values reduce false positives in legitimate security discussion.
contextDiscount.operationalMaxDiscountHint: Maximum reduction after execution, delivery, theft, or evasion intent is present. Zero is recommended so a research disclaimer cannot cancel explicit harmful action.

promptFilter.terminalCategoriesCollapsedDesc: Configure terminal categories and audit models that a clean secondary review may release.
promptFilter.riskSimplifiedDesc: Accumulates periodic user, IP, and session risk; disabled by default.
promptFilter.outputSimplifiedDesc: Scans streaming output for strict high-risk signals; disabled by default.

extensions.title: Deep Protection Extensions
extensions.collapsedDesc: Sidecar, session correlation, attachment parsing, and scheduled intelligence stay hidden until their services and identity paths are ready.
extensions.runtimeLimits: Runtime Limits, Cache, and Circuit Breaker

sidecar.title: Semantic Review Sidecar
sidecar.description: Connect a local or private semantic model to supplement rule matching. It is disabled and set to Shadow by default so quality can be measured before warnings or blocks are enabled.
sidecar.enabledHint: Enable only after a controlled Sidecar URL is configured. No external call is made while disabled.
sidecar.scanCleanHint: Review a deterministic sample of requests that local rules allowed to find semantic misses. Disabled by default to control latency and cost.
sidecar.modeHint: Shadow records only, Warn returns a notice, and Enforce allows Sidecar decisions to block. Calibrate in Shadow first.
sidecar.baseURLHint: Fixed root URL of a local or private semantic-review service. Never source it from user input.
sidecar.timeoutHint: Maximum wait for one semantic review before applying the failure policy.
sidecar.minScoreHint: Call the Sidecar when the local enforcement score reaches this value. Sampled clean requests bypass this threshold.
sidecar.samplePercentHint: Applies only to locally allowed requests. Start at 1%–10% instead of sending all normal traffic to the model.
sidecar.failClosedHint: Treat a timeout or Sidecar error as a failure that may block. Keep off by default so an extension outage does not take down normal traffic.
sidecar.maxTextLengthHint: Upper limit sent to the Sidecar. Oversized content keeps bounded head and tail sections to protect resources.
sidecar.cacheTTLHint: How long to reuse a semantic decision for identical content. Set to zero to disable caching.
sidecar.maxConcurrentHint: Maximum simultaneous Sidecar calls, preventing the semantic service from being overloaded.
sidecar.breakerFailuresHint: Temporarily stop Sidecar calls after this many consecutive failures.
sidecar.breakerSecondsHint: How long the circuit remains open before automatic recovery is attempted.

session.title: Session Fragment Correlation
session.description: Join explicit continuation requests with recent fragments from the same trusted session to detect instructions deliberately split across turns.
session.enabledHint: Session writes still access the cache synchronously and may add request latency. Keep this off for now.
session.requireSignedIdentityHint: Use only user and session identifiers verified by NewAPI HMAC, preventing clients from forging another session.
session.combineShortFragmentsHint: Join short fragments even without an explicit continuation phrase. Keep off to avoid linking unrelated normal messages.
session.windowHint: Only fragments from the same session inside this window are eligible. Longer windows increase cross-task correlation risk.
session.maxFragmentsHint: Maximum number of recent fragments included in one combined inspection, bounding work and context drift.
session.maxTextLengthHint: Maximum total length of current and historical text; excess content is bounded and truncated.
session.shortFragmentMaxCharsHint: Used only when automatic short-message joining is enabled. Longer messages are not auto-joined as ordinary fragments.
session.recommendedHint: Recommended default: correlation off, signed identity still required, and ordinary short-message joining off. Enable it after ordered asynchronous writes are available so cache latency stays off the first-token path.

attachment.title: Attachment Content Extraction
attachment.description: Send supported attachment references to a separate extractor, then inspect the returned text. Codex2API does not fetch arbitrary user URLs directly; this layer is disabled and Shadowed by default.
attachment.enabledHint: Enable only after deploying a controlled extraction service. Attachment reference metadata can still be inspected while this is off.
attachment.allowRemoteURLsHint: Remote fetching adds SSRF, oversized-file, and mutable-content risk. Keep off and accept only trusted file references by default.
attachment.baseURLHint: Fixed root URL for the local or private attachment extractor. Requests must not override it dynamically.
attachment.timeoutHint: Maximum wait for extraction. Failures are audited and should not block normal traffic by default.
attachment.maxFilesHint: Maximum number of attachments submitted to the extractor for one request.
attachment.maxBytesHint: Per-file size limit used to contain oversized files and decompression bombs.
attachment.maxExtractedCharsHint: Maximum extracted attachment text returned to prompt inspection; excess text is truncated.
attachment.cacheTTLHint: How long extracted content is cached by file digest. Set to zero to disable caching.
attachment.maxConcurrentHint: Maximum simultaneous extraction calls so the parser cannot stall the main proxy.
attachment.breakerFailuresHint: Temporarily stop extractor calls after this many consecutive failures.
attachment.breakerSecondsHint: How long extraction remains paused before an automatic recovery probe.

promptFilter.terminalCategoriesHint: Comma-separated. A category enters terminal handling only when its rule also forms a high-confidence violation above threshold. Do not add dual-use categories such as reverse engineering or vulnerabilities.
promptFilter.terminalBypassModelsHint: Comma-separated exact requested model IDs. For these models only, a successful clean secondary review may clear a local terminal match. Review errors or flagged results remain blocked.
promptFilter.localBlockMessagePlaceholder: Request contains content blocked by prompt filter
promptFilter.conversationLockEnabled: Lock the current conversation after upstream CYB
promptFilter.cybStrikeEnabled: Allow upstream CYB to count toward account suspension
promptFilter.localSevereStrikeEnabled: Accrue CYB ban on local severe violations

help.normalizationPanel: Bounded decoding restores common encoded and compressed fragments while byte, block, and pass limits prevent decoding bombs from exhausting the service.
help.normalizationEnabled: Normalize full-width characters, Unicode confusables, and invisible characters before matching rules.
help.decodeRuns: Maximum nested decoding passes. One or two is recommended to limit latency.
help.maxDecodedBytes: Maximum bytes produced by all decoding attempts for one request; further decoding stops at this budget.
help.maxEncodedBlocks: Maximum independent encoded fragments decoded in one request, limiting many-small-block resource abuse.
help.decodeUrl: Detect URL-encoded bypasses such as percent escapes and query encoding.
help.decodeHtml: Detect HTML entity and numeric entity encoding bypasses.
help.decodeBase64: Decode Base64-like prompt fragments before inspection.
help.decodeHex: Restore continuous hexadecimal and 0x-style fragments within the configured byte budget.
help.decodeRot13: Consider structurally plausible ROT13 text and inspect only meaningful decoded results.
help.decodeEscapes: Restore Unicode, hexadecimal, and common backslash escape sequences.
help.decodeCompression: Inspect Base64-wrapped gzip or zlib text within the configured size and pass limits.
help.terminalCategories: A listed category enters terminal handling only with independent high-confidence harmful intent above the block threshold. Keep this empty unless the whole category has very low false-positive risk.
help.terminalBypassModels: Use only for dedicated audit models whose prompts intentionally contain policy violations. Matching uses the requested model ID, not a mapped upstream model.
help.localBlockMessage: Shown only when the local Prompt Filter directly blocks a request. Upstream policy, conversation-lock, and cooldown messages are unchanged.
help.conversationLockEnabled: Locks only after an explicit upstream cyber_policy response with a stable signed session fingerprint. Locked retries never add strikes, and requests without a reliable conversation identity are not guessed or locked.
help.conversationLockTTL: Automatically unlocks after this lifetime. A new upstream CYB decision can lock the conversation again. Defaults to 168 hours, capped at 720 hours.
help.userCyberCooldownMinutes: How long the same verified user remains blocked after upstream CYB even if they change sessions. Defaults to 30 minutes and accepts 1–1440 minutes; errors and risk profiles use the configured remaining time.
help.cybStrikeEnabled: Disabled by default. When enabled, only explicit upstream cyber_policy decisions are signed as countable. When disabled, they are still audited, reported, and may lock the conversation, but NewAPI will not count them or automatically suspend the account.
help.authorizedPentestAllowed: Off (default): unverifiable claims such as an asserted written authorization or an "this is my own server" statement no longer exempt a request from the terminal targeted-intrusion rule, closing a one-sentence bypass. On: restores the previous allow behaviour - enable only if your deployment genuinely serves authorized penetration testing. Requests with no authorization claim, and purely defensive requests, are unaffected.
help.localSevereStrikeEnabled: On (default): a highest-confidence severe violation sent directly by the current user (targeted intrusion, malware, and similar terminal hits) is blocked locally and also records one CYB strike against the NewAPI user, driving the automatic ban once the threshold is reached - without the request first reaching the upstream and producing a real cyber_policy. Repeats within a locked conversation do not re-accrue, and low-confidence blocks, tool output, and history context never accrue, keeping the false-ban surface at the highest-confidence tier. Off: severe violations are still blocked but record no strike (blocking is decoupled from banning).
help.riskEnabled: Track recent confirmed user, IP, and session risk for audit and review prioritization. Historical risk alone never blocks a later request.
help.riskWindow: How long risk history is retained before older scores decay.
help.blockThreshold: Reference line for high accumulated risk; it never blocks the current request without independent evidence.
help.reviewThreshold: Reference line for a Sidecar or future semantic reviewer to prioritize review. The current request still needs its own violation evidence.
help.outputEnabled: Buffer and inspect SSE or WebSocket content before sending it to the client.
help.strictOnly: Only terminal strict rules interrupt output, reducing ordinary-text false positives.
help.bufferBytes: Maximum amount buffered for each output inspection pass.
help.overlapBytes: Content retained between frames to detect dangerous phrases split across multiple deltas.
help.scheduleEnabled: Automatically run public intelligence searches at the configured interval.
help.intervalHours: Minimum number of hours between automatic intelligence runs.
help.maxResults: Maximum public projects saved and supplied to the analysis model per run.
help.modelEnabled: Use a model from the current Codex2API account pool to generate candidate rules.
help.model: Pool model used for intelligence analysis.
help.maxModelCalls: Maximum pool-model requests per run, from zero to three.
help.queries: Custom queries, one per line. They are merged with and deduplicated against built-in queries.

promptFilter.sensitiveWordsPlaceholder: One term per line. A match is an audit signal; blocking still requires explicit harmful intent or a matching compound rule.
promptFilter.sensitiveWordsHint: Sensitive words are audit signals only and never raise the enforcement score. Use a custom intent or strict rule when a specific combination must be blocked.
promptFilter.reviewDesc: When enabled, requests selected by the review scope are evaluated by the configured provider. Local rules remain independent evidence.
promptFilter.reviewScopeHint: External review scope is explicit and independent from the local preset. Review traffic may include user content, so evaluate latency, quota, privacy, and the failure policy before enabling it.
promptFilter.reviewProfilesHint: Save the Base URL, model, adapter, and key count without replacing the active configuration. Activate a profile to switch. Keys are never returned to the page.
promptFilter.reviewProfileDeleteConfirm: Delete review profile “{{name}}”? The active configuration will not be changed.
promptFilter.reviewApiKeyPlaceholder: One key per line (sk-...), multiple allowed
promptFilter.reviewApiKeyConfigured: {{n}} key(s) configured; leave blank to keep
promptFilter.reviewApiKeyHint: One key per line. Multiple keys are round-robin balanced and failed over on rate limits, invalid keys, or server errors.
promptFilter.reviewKeyListHint: Only masked saved keys are shown. The list refreshes after saving, and connection test status maps back to each saved key.
promptFilter.reviewKeyDeleteConfirm: This removes {{key}} without changing the other review keys. The last key cannot be deleted while model review is enabled.
promptFilter.reviewKeyRemoveDraftAria: Remove review key {{key}} from the pending list
promptFilter.reviewKeyRemovedFromDraft: Removed {{key}} from the pending list; save settings to apply the change
promptFilter.reviewKeyRemovedFromDraftEmpty: Removed {{key}}; the pending list is now empty, so saving keeps the currently configured keys unchanged
promptFilter.moderationThresholdsHint: A Moderations category is matched when its score is greater than or equal to the configured threshold. The provider's flagged boolean is not used for enforcement.
promptFilter.reviewResilienceDesc: Usually no tuning is needed. Repeated failures stop synchronous waits, and one probe is allowed after the recovery window.
promptFilter.reviewSystemPromptHint: Immutable review instructions. The model should emit only confidence and reason JSON.
promptFilter.reviewSystemPromptPlaceholder: Leave blank to use the server-managed default prompt
promptFilter.reviewUserPromptTemplateHint: Must contain {{text}}. The server safely substitutes it inside the <user_input> wrapper.
promptFilter.reviewUserPromptTemplatePlaceholder: Leave blank to use the server-managed input wrapper
promptFilter.reviewPayloadTemplateHint: Leave blank for the built-in adapter. Custom JSON supports {{model}}, {{system_prompt}}, {{user_prompt}}, and {{text}}; substitution occurs after JSON parsing.
promptFilter.reviewConnectionTestDesc: Sends one real review with the current unsaved Base URL, model, prompts, and payload. A blank API key uses the stored key.
promptFilter.reviewTestSuccess: Review connection and JSON parsing succeeded
promptFilter.executionScoreHint: The enforcement score and current threshold determine whether this request enters the warning or blocking flow. A model review may also block when the enforcement score is 0.
promptFilter.shadowAuditScoreHint: The shadow audit score does not participate in current blocking.
promptFilter.reviewModelsFetchHint: Fetch the provider model list using the current base URL and API key
promptFilter.reviewModelsEmpty: The provider returned an empty model list
promptFilter.legacyMissingMatchContext: This older record did not save the matched excerpt. New records created after the upgrade will show it here.
promptFilter.keywordPlaceholder: Search preview, matches, error code, or key
promptFilter.auditRecordsCount: {{incidents}} CY incidents, {{reviews}} model reviews, {{logs}} local audit logs

docs.title: Prompt Filter Guide
docs.description: How the Prompt Filter works, what each tab is for, recommended activation steps, and how to use advanced protection, secondary review, intelligence, and NewAPI audit integration.

what.title: What this module does
what.p1: Prompt Filter inspects user prompts before they reach upstream models. It aims to catch jailbreaks, injection, malware help, credential theft, reverse engineering, and similar high-risk content while limiting false positives.
what.p2: It is a gateway policy layer: deterministic local rules score the request first, then the selected mode decides monitor / warn / block. Optional layers add decoding, cumulative risk, output scanning, and NewAPI audit integration.
what.b1: Local rules: intent-bearing built-in/custom patterns produce the enforcement score; sensitive words and signal-only patterns remain audit evidence.
what.b2: Modes: monitor logs only, warn can pass through, block rejects the request.
what.b3: Terminal rules still pass intent, effective-score, and context checks. When full model review is enabled, terminal candidates enter the same review path.
what.b4: Observability: hit logs store action, score, matched rules, and content preview for triage.

pipeline.title: Request pipeline
pipeline.p1: A request is processed roughly in this order (advanced layers are off by default):
pipeline.s1: Accept the request and extract text up to the configured max length.
pipeline.s2: Optional: normalize input and decode URL / HTML / Base64 encodings.
pipeline.s3: Match local rules: sensitive words and signal-only topics enter audit scoring, while intent-bearing built-in/custom rules enter enforcement scoring.
pipeline.s4: Evaluate score thresholds, strict threshold, terminal strict, and terminal categories.
pipeline.s5: Optional: accumulate user / IP / session risk. With full model review enabled, every extractable current-user input calls a Moderations- or Chat-Completions-compatible endpoint.
pipeline.s6: Emit allow / warn / block; requests using NewAPI audit integration also receive signed policy events for the caller to handle according to its own configuration.
pipeline.s7: Optional: buffer and scan SSE / WebSocket output so risky content in model replies is still caught.

pages.title: How to use each tab
pages.p1: There are five tabs. A good order is configure → rules → verify → operate → intelligence.
pages.overview: Master switch, mode, thresholds, sensitive words, advanced protection, secondary review, tester, and recent hits.
pages.logs: Search all hit records by action, source, endpoint, model, and API key.
pages.rules: Enable/disable built-in rules, manage custom rules, and test regex hits.
pages.intelligence: Search public signals for candidate rules and add them after human review.
pages.docs: This usage guide and activation checklist.

quickstart.title: Quick start (recommended)
quickstart.p1: Fresh installs include a low-false-positive blocking preset. Test it with real normal and violating prompts before enabling the master switch; high-volume existing sites can still canary in Monitor mode.
quickstart.s1: Keep the preset Block mode, 50 / 90 thresholds, terminal strict handling, two-pass normalization, and match logging.
quickstart.s2: Choose sensible thresholds (for example 50 / 90) and watch score distribution in logs.
quickstart.s3: On Rules, keep critical intent and terminal rules enabled; add business-specific sensitive words as audit signals (one per line).
quickstart.s4: Use the rule tester with real production prompts and confirm false positives are acceptable.
quickstart.s5: Enable the master switch after validation. Existing high-volume sites may use Monitor or Warn for a 1–3 day canary.
quickstart.s6: Enable cumulative risk, secondary review, output scanning, Sidecar, and intelligence independently when their dependencies are ready.
quickstart.callout: Fresh installs include a general production preset: block mode, 50 / 90 thresholds, terminal strict handling, and two-pass input normalization once the master switch is enabled. Secondary review, output scanning, and external services remain opt-in.

modes.title: Processing modes
modes.p1: Mode controls gateway behavior after scoring; it does not disable scoring itself.
modes.monitor: Log only; do not change request allow path. Best for initial tuning.
modes.warn: Log and mark a warning; request usually continues upstream. Good for canary.
modes.block: Reject when thresholds or terminal hits fire. Use for production hard enforcement.
modes.callout: In block/enforce mode, strict:true rules still pass intent, effective-score, and context checks. Full model review applies the same review and failure policy to every extractable current-user input.

scoring.title: Scoring, thresholds, and terminal hits
scoring.p1: Each matched rule adds its weight. Ordinary decisions use the block threshold; strict rules also use the strict threshold.
scoring.p2: Terminal paths still require high-confidence harmful intent. Rule scores and context discounts are applied first; strict rules or terminal categories become terminal only after the effective score reaches the block threshold.
scoring.b1: Block threshold: cumulative score that triggers the mode action (block in block mode).
scoring.b2: Strict threshold: cumulative strict-rule score that can also trigger handling.
scoring.b3: Terminal strict blocking starts after intent and effective-score checks pass; when full model review is enabled it still receives the unified model verdict.
scoring.b4: Terminal categories: become terminal only with a high-confidence violation; avoid assigning dual-use technology categories.

advanced.title: Advanced protection
advanced.p1: Fresh installs enable input normalization by default. Cumulative risk, Sidecar, output scanning, online intelligence, and NewAPI integration remain independent opt-in layers.
advanced.b1: Normalization & decoding: full-width/confusable cleanup and URL/HTML/Base64 unwrapping.
advanced.b2: Terminal categories: take the terminal path only after the category forms a high-confidence violation.
advanced.b3: User / IP / session risk: records confirmed high-risk events for audit and review; cumulative score alone never bans.
advanced.b4: SSE / WebSocket output scan: inspect streamed model output; can limit to terminal rules only.
advanced.b5: NewAPI audit integration: verify signed identity and policy metadata only through one-to-one Codex2API Key bindings; unbound Keys cannot accept identity.
advanced.b6: Scheduled intelligence: periodic public search and optional candidate rule generation.
advanced.callout: Use Redis-backed cache for multi-replica cumulative risk. Keep decode runs at 1–2 to control latency. Output scanning holds a small window for cross-frame detection: when combined with preflight passthrough (codex_preflight_sse_passthrough), tiny metadata frames may still be briefly buffered so first-frame speed is not guaranteed to recover; and once HTTP 200 is committed before the first content event, upstream error status-code recovery changes — grayscale the two together.

review.title: Full model review
review.p1: With the master switch and model review enabled, every extractable current-user input is reviewed before forwarding. Local rules remain parallel evidence and no longer gate model calls.
review.p2: Supports Moderations and Chat Completions adapters with configurable base URL, model, agent prompt, input wrapper, payload JSON, confidence threshold, concurrency, timeout, multiple API keys, and failure policy.
review.b1: Block on failure: conservative production default when review times out or errors.
review.b2: Allow on failure: keep traffic flowing if review is unavailable (canary).
review.b3: A flagged model verdict can block a locally clean request; a clear verdict can remove a local false positive. Errors follow the configured fail-open or fail-closed policy.

rules.title: Working with the rule set
rules.p1: Built-in rules can be toggled by category in batch. Extra rules live in system settings and can be added, edited, or removed independently.
rules.p2: Custom rules use Go regex. Names must be unique; weight is the score on match; strict marks a strong rule; prefer stable English categories.
rules.b1: Use strict or terminal categories only for very low false-positive high-risk patterns.
rules.b2: Dual-use phrases should stay non-strict with moderate weight, relying on thresholds and review.
rules.b3: Validate with both the rules regex tester and the overview prompt tester before relying on a rule.
rules.b4: Advanced composite rules may use all_patterns / any_patterns / exclude_patterns.

logs.title: Reading hit logs
logs.p1: Logs support tuning and incident review. Overview shows the latest five hits; full search is on the Hit Logs tab.
logs.b1: Action: allow / warn / block is the final decision.
logs.b2: Source: local rules, upstream cyber_policy, intelligence jobs (intel_*), etc.
logs.b3: Score and matches: which rules contributed to the score.
logs.b4: Filter by endpoint, model, API key, and keyword; open full request text when needed.

intelligence.title: Rule intelligence
intelligence.p1: The intelligence tab searches public GitHub-style sources for jailbreak/injection signals and can optionally use a pool model to draft candidate regex rules.
intelligence.b1: Public intelligence and upstream risk feedback enter one persistent review queue and never affect scoring directly.
intelligence.b2: Scheduled search and model calls must be explicitly enabled under Advanced Protection.
intelligence.b3: Administrator publish is the only way a candidate enters runtime rules; dismissing does not erase historical evidence.
intelligence.callout: The review queue is not a second rule engine. Published rules enter the existing custom rule set and use the same validation, scoring, and enforcement path.

newapi.title: NewAPI audit integration
newapi.p1: When NewAPI relays traffic to Codex2API, it signs the user ID, IP, request ID, request-body digest, and policy metadata. Codex2API verifies those signatures before associating audit identity and policy.
newapi.p2: Every caller must use the binding for the Codex2API Key that carries its requests. Retired process-wide secret configuration no longer participates in verification. Header and signature details are available under NewAPI Audit Integration on the overview page.
newapi.b1: Each binding has its own secret and enabled state. Unbound Keys cannot accept NewAPI signed identity.
newapi.b2: Auditing, warnings, account restrictions, and IP restrictions remain separate NewAPI controls and must not be enabled automatically by identity verification.
newapi.b3: NewAPI must sign request headers, verify signed Codex2API policy events, and persist audit records according to its own configuration.

checklist.title: Go-live checklist
checklist.p1: Run through this list before production cutover to reduce false blocks and misses.
checklist.s1: Master switch on; mode graduated from monitor to block.
checklist.s2: Enforcement thresholds, terminal strict rules, audit-only sensitive words, and core built-in rules reviewed.
checklist.s3: Tester coverage includes normal business samples and attack samples.
checklist.s4: Secondary review keys/timeout/fail policy configured and failure-path exercised.
checklist.s5: Enable decoding, cumulative risk, and output scan only as needed; multi-replica cache ready.
checklist.s6: Logs are searchable and review workflows are clear; NewAPI secrets and ban policy aligned if used.

responseCache.title: Response context cache
responseCache.description: Bound this instance's retained Responses continuation context and Redis reconstruction size.
responseCache.totalDesc: Integer from 8 to 4096 MiB. Changes apply live and may immediately evict least-recently-used entries.
responseCache.entryDesc: Integer from 1 to 256 MiB and no greater than the local total budget.
responseCache.reconstructDesc: Integer from 8 to 512 MiB. Bounds the logical context reconstructed for one continuation.
responseCache.l1Note: The default 8 MiB entry value is an L1 admission limit. With Redis, a larger context may still continue up to the reconstruction limit, but it is not promoted into local L1.
responseCache.memoryNote: In Memory mode, an oversize or evicted context cannot be recovered from another backend. A dependent continuation may return HTTP 409 response_context_unavailable.

settings.autoCleanUnauthorizedDesc: Checks every 30 seconds and removes accounts with unauthorized status.
settings.autoCleanRateLimitedDesc: Checks every 30 seconds and removes accounts with rate_limited status.
settings.autoCleanFullUsageDesc: Checks every 5 minutes and removes accounts with ≥ 100% usage. Accounts with active requests are skipped.
settings.autoCleanErrorDesc: Checks every 30 seconds and removes accounts in error state (e.g. expired refresh tokens).
settings.autoCleanExpiredDesc: Every 15 minutes, removes accounts older than 30 minutes regardless of usage. Runs immediately when toggled on.
settings.schedulingAccountGroupDesc: Decides which account each new request lands on: the fast scheduler provides in-memory indexed dispatch, and the scheduler mode picks the distribution strategy on top of it.
settings.schedulingAffinityGroupDesc: Whether follow-up requests in the same conversation reuse the same account, plus hash-based spreading when multiple users share one key.
settings.schedulerModeRequiresFast: Only takes effect while the fast scheduler is enabled.
settings.connectivityTestDesc: Probe configuration used by the Test button on the accounts page: probe model, batch test concurrency, and request content.
settings.siteNameDesc: Shown in the sidebar, login page, and browser title so multiple deployments are easy to tell apart.
settings.siteLogoDesc: PNG, JPG, or SVG. Max 600KB. 80x80px square images are recommended; larger uploads are compressed proportionally.
settings.siteLogoInvalidType: Only PNG, JPG, or SVG files are supported
settings.siteLogoTooLarge: Could not compress this image below 600KB. Please choose a smaller image.
settings.siteLogoCompressionFailed: Automatic compression failed. Please choose a PNG, JPG, or SVG under 600KB.
settings.timezoneDesc: Controls date/time display in the frontend. The page will reload automatically after changing.
settings.showFullUsageNumbersDesc: When enabled, Usage and API Keys → Token Usage show full request/token counts. When disabled, they use compact units like 1.2K and 3.4M.
settings.fastSchedulerEnabledDesc: Uses an in-memory fast scheduling algorithm, significantly reducing dispatch latency under high concurrency. Recommended for large account pools (100+).
settings.codexWebsocketDesc: Controls the persistent WebSocket connection between the proxy and the Codex upstream. All options are off by default and do not affect the existing HTTP request path.
settings.codexForceWebsocketDesc: When enabled, requests to the Codex upstream use a persistent WebSocket (with connection pooling), cutting per-request TLS/handshake overhead to better match the official CLI. Disabled by default; when off, requests use the existing HTTP path.
settings.codexWSWeakNetworkModeDesc: For unstable VPN or residential-proxy links: rotate connections after 15 seconds idle or 3 minutes total, and require a real Ping/Pong before every reuse. Idle keepalive is paused while enabled. Disabled by default.
settings.codexWSKeepaliveEnabledDesc: When enabled, a background task periodically sends Ping frames to already-established idle upstream WebSocket connections (no new requests, no account quota usage) to reduce cold-start latency on reuse. Paused while weak-network mode is enabled. Disabled by default.
settings.codexWSKeepaliveIntervalDesc: Interval in seconds between WebSocket keepalive Pings, range 10–600, default 60. Only effective when WS Keepalive is enabled.
settings.codexWSHideUpstreamErrorsDesc: When enabled, clients receive one friendly fallback message after final WS upstream failure while raw upstream errors remain in backend logs and usage records. Enabled by default.
settings.codexWSSilentRetryEnabledDesc: When enabled, rate limits, usage exhaustion, 5xx, read errors, and timeouts before the first token switch accounts and rebuild the upstream WS while the client connection keeps waiting. Enabled by default.
settings.codexWSSizeRouterEnabledDesc: Learns the trigger size from actual WS close 1009 (message too big) events and sends later requests of similar size straight to the HTTP upstream, avoiding the first-token delay of waiting for a doomed WS attempt before the serial fallback. Learned threshold expires after 6 hours and recalibrates. Enabled by default.
settings.codexWSBusyAcquireMaxWaitDesc: Concurrent requests of the same session queue for the in-use WS connection; once the cumulative wait exceeds this cap the attempt fails and retries on another account. Default 30s.
settings.codexWSBusyOverflowEnabledDesc: When queueing outlasts the patience below, reuse or create a bounded sibling connection on the same account and send immediately, removing the fixed ~30s first-token tail. The request's prompt_cache_key is unchanged, so upstream caching is unaffected. Disabled by default.
settings.codexWSBusyPatienceDesc: Seconds to wait for the original connection to go idle before overflowing: requests finishing within a short gap still reuse it and keep connection locality. Default 2s.
settings.codexOverloadPauseDesc: Per-account stats on upstream server_is_overloaded errors: when their share within a sliding window reaches the threshold, the account is paused from scheduling and resumes automatically. Codex channel only.
settings.codexOverloadPauseEnabledDesc: Requires at least 5 requests in the window before judging, so low-traffic accounts are not tripped by a single error; tripped accounts show "Upstream overload paused" with a resume countdown.
settings.codexOverloadThresholdDesc: Trips when overloaded errors reach this share of requests in the window. Default 20%.
settings.codexOverloadPauseMinutesDesc: How long scheduling is paused after tripping. Default 30 minutes; resumes automatically.
settings.githubAccessDesc: Dedicated config for features that reach GitHub (CLI version sync, pricing sync, online update). A token solves shared-IP API rate limits (60 req/h).
settings.githubTokenDesc: Personal Access Token (no scopes needed); raises the API quota to 5000 req/h. Sent only to api.github.com — never to mirrors or other hosts. Not echoed back after saving.
settings.githubTokenPlaceholder: Not configured — paste a token to save
settings.githubTokenConfiguredPlaceholder: Configured (enter a new value to replace)
settings.githubProxyDesc: Outbound proxy applied only to github.com / api.github.com / *.githubusercontent.com, decoupled from the global proxy. Empty falls back to the global proxy (online update falls back to env proxy).
settings.codexWSStatelessSlotsDesc: Persistent WS connection slots per (account, cache key) for stateless requests (1-32, default 8). Higher: more idle connections per account; lower: more handshakes, which may trip upstream handshake rate limits at high RPM. Effective value is still capped by the account's dynamic concurrency limit. Hot-reloads.
settings.codexWSSilentMaxRetriesDesc: Maximum account-switch retries for upstream WS errors before the first token, range 0-10, default 2.
settings.schedulerModeDesc: Scheduling priority is segmented first; health tier, dispatch score, and current load decide within the same priority. Round Robin favors even distribution, Remaining Quota prefers lower usage, and Fill First keeps draining one account until it is exhausted or rate-limited before moving to the next.
settings.affinityModeDesc: Affinity is separate from scheduling priority. With a shared API key, send X-Codex2API-Affinity-Key to distinguish end users; it is hashed and used locally only. Bounded rotates after 50 requests, 5 minutes, or unhealthy status; Off re-picks; Strict stays long-term.
settings.sessionAffinitySpreadDesc: When a new affinity key binds for the first time, pick the account by deterministic hashing within the same priority and health tier instead of always taking the current top score: the same key always maps to the same account, different keys spread evenly, and an unavailable pick falls through in hash order. Off keeps the classic top-score behavior. Multi-replica deployments converge without coordination.
settings.grokSettingsDesc: Settings specific to the Grok (xAI) upstream. Grok's prompt cache is per-account and prefix-based, so stronger session affinity means better cache reuse and lower cost/latency.
settings.grokAffinityModeDesc: Applies to Grok accounts only, overriding the global affinity mode above. Grok's cached-read hits are per-account+prefix; switching accounts mid-conversation invalidates the cache (cached read drops to one block = 128 tokens). Default Strict keeps a conversation on one account long-term to maximize cache reuse; Follow uses the global mode; Bounded/Off match the global semantics.
settings.grokProbeEnabledDesc: When enabled, a background task re-runs a connectivity test against every enabled Grok account at the interval below and writes back status: OK clears cooldown to active; 429 records a usage snapshot per free-quota-exhaustion semantics and marks it rate-limited. Corrects drift from the real state during idle periods (e.g. after a restart, or exhaustion/recovery within the upstream rolling window). Note: probing sends a small real request upstream, consuming a little free quota per cycle on free accounts. Off by default.
settings.grokProbeIntervalDesc: Minimum interval between probe rounds, at least 5, default 30. Shorter is more timely but consumes more quota and adds upstream load.
settings.grokMaxRateLimitRetriesDesc: When a Grok request hits a rate limit (429 / free-quota exhausted), the account is marked rate-limited (excluded from scheduling while cooling down) and the request is automatically retried on another available account, up to this many times. Applies to Grok accounts only. 0 = follow the global rate-limit retries. Grok free accounts hit limits often, so raising this can improve success rate.
settings.grokFollowUpEffortEnabledDesc: Off by default. When enabled, Claude Code on Grok still uses high/xhigh for the first user turn, and drops tool-result follow-ups and tiny no-tools requests one step. grok-4.6 has low/medium/high/xhigh; grok-4.5 tops out at high.
settings.grokFollowUpToolEffortDesc: Reasoning effort for turns that already include tool_result. Default medium: the tool is chosen, Grok only needs to read the result and continue.
settings.grokFollowUpSmallEffortDesc: Reasoning effort for tiny requests with no tools and no assistant history (for example a parallel title/summary call). Default low.
settings.grokOAuthClientIdDesc: OAuth client_id used for Grok authorization (browser flow, device code, SSO conversion, token refresh). Empty = the built-in official Grok CLI public id. Existing accounts keep refreshing with the client_id stored in their own credentials, so this only affects authorizations created from now on. The GROK_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID environment variable takes precedence over this setting.
settings.grokOAuthClientIdEnvOverride: Currently pinned to {{value}} by the GROK_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID environment variable; this setting has no effect. Clear that variable and restart to use the value configured here.
settings.allowRemoteMigrationDesc: When enabled, other codex2api instances can pull healthy accounts from this instance.
settings.allowRemoteMigrationRequiresSecret: Set an admin secret first. Remote migration cannot be enabled without admin authentication.
settings.resinDesc: When configured, all account requests are routed through Resin reverse proxy for sticky IP binding per account. Both fields must be set to enable; clear to disable.
settings.resinUrlDesc: Resin proxy pool address with token, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:2260/my-token
settings.resinPlatformNameDesc: Platform identifier in Resin, used to distinguish different services. e.g. codex2api
settings.adminSecretPlaceholder: Leave empty to disable admin auth
settings.adminSecretDesc: When set, all /api/admin/* endpoints require X-Admin-Key header. Leave empty to disable.
settings.adminSecretEnvOverride: ADMIN_SECRET is currently enabled in the environment, so admin login uses the environment value first.
settings.promptFilterEnabledDesc: System-level switch. Detailed rules live in the Prompt Filter page.
settings.promptFilterModeDesc: Monitor only records, warn passes through, block rejects requests.
settings.modelsDesc: The following models are currently available:
settings.deleteKeyDesc: After deletion, all clients using this key will immediately lose access. Please confirm.
settings.noKeysDesc: API requires no auth without keys. Generated keys will appear here.
settings.keyAuthNote: API requires no auth without keys. After adding the first key, all /v1/* requests need Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx
settings.maxConcurrencyRange: Max concurrent requests per account (min 1, no upper limit)
settings.maxRetriesRange: Retry account switches for transport errors, 5xx, and 401 (0~10), 0 = no retry
settings.retryIntervalMsDesc: Wait between retry attempts (0~30000), 0 = retry immediately. 2000+ recommended for flaky networks
settings.transportRetryPolicyDesc: How to retry connection-level failures (network blips, proxy node switches): sticky = keep the same account without penalizing it, wait the interval, retry
settings.maxRateLimitRetriesRange: Maximum account switches after a 429 rate limit (0~10), 0 = return the 429 directly
settings.testModelHint: Model used for account connection testing
settings.testContentDesc: User input sent upstream by single tests, batch tests, and background probes. With multiple lines, one is picked at random each time; supports variables like {{time}}, {{date}}, {{rand}}, {{rand:1-100}}. Empty values fall back to hi.
settings.backgroundRefreshIntervalDesc: Controls how often RT refresh, usage probe batches, and recovery probes are triggered, in minutes (1~1440). Saving resets the timer to the new interval.
settings.usageProbeMaxAgeDesc: Runs another usage probe only after the snapshot is older than this many minutes; lazy mode uses wham only (1~10080).
settings.usageProbeConcurrencyDesc: Maximum parallel usage probes (1~128, default 16). Raising it speeds up sampling for large pools but may trigger upstream rate limits.
settings.usageProbeResponsesFallbackDesc: Allow a real /responses probe when wham usage lookup fails. Disable for wham-only sampling; lazy mode always skips this fallback.
settings.recoveryProbeIntervalDesc: Minimum gap between recovery probes for banned accounts, in minutes (1~10080).
settings.lazyModeDesc: Disables proactive account refreshes and real responses probes. RT accounts refresh AT only when dispatched; usage keeps zero-cost wham sampling plus real-request updates.
settings.runtimeOptimizationDesc: Control legacy Codex client compatibility, usage-log disk writes, stream flush cadence, and first-token timeout retries.
settings.clientCompatModeDesc: preserve is the default and keeps the client UA; auto upgrades only outdated Codex CLI/TUI UA; force always uses a server-generated UA.
settings.codexMinCliVersionDesc: Auto mode replacement threshold. Structured generated UA versions below this are raised to this version; raw UA override remains exact.
settings.codexCliVersionSyncDesc: Fetch the latest stable version from openai/codex releases to raise the emulated version in outbound UA / manifest (never downgrades), so upstream version gates can be followed without a release. Auto-syncs every 12h by default; set CODEX_DISABLE_CLI_VERSION_SYNC=1 to disable.
settings.codexCliVersionAutoSyncDesc: When on, the emulated version is fetched and updated in the background at the interval below; when off, only manual "Sync now" remains. CODEX_DISABLE_CLI_VERSION_SYNC=1 forces it off.
settings.codexCliVersionSyncIntervalDesc: Wait time between automatic syncs (hours, range 1-720).
settings.codexUserAgentRawDesc: Optional exact header value. Leave blank to build from the fields below. Version segments are rebuilt to the current effective Codex CLI version on egress.
settings.codexUAClientNameDesc: Client token before the slash and in the trailing marker.
settings.codexUAClientVersionDesc: Version emitted in the generated UA. In auto mode, values below the minimum CLI version are raised to that threshold.
settings.codexUAOSNameDesc: First platform token, for example Mac OS, Linux, Ubuntu, or Windows.
settings.codexUAOSVersionDesc: Second platform token, for example 13.7.8, Unknown, or 24.04.
settings.codexUAArchDesc: Architecture token in the platform block, such as arm64 or x86_64.
settings.codexUATerminalDesc: TERM_PROGRAM or TERM value, such as xterm-256color.
settings.usageLogModeDesc: full records all requests; errors records failures only; off disables usage_logs writes to reduce disk pressure.
settings.usageLogBatchSizeDesc: Write logs to the database once the buffer reaches this size (1~1000; 200~500 recommended for 5k RPM).
settings.usageLogFlushIntervalDesc: When the batch size is not reached, write at least once every N seconds (1~300).
settings.billingTierPolicyDesc: actual bills by the upstream-reported response.service_tier (falls back to the requested intent when upstream reports none); requested preserves the old behavior and bills explicit fast/priority requests as Fast. Note: on the ChatGPT OAuth path upstream may always report default even when Fast is actually applied — the reported value alone cannot prove a request was not accelerated.
settings.streamFlushPolicyDesc: immediate flushes every SSE event; coalesce briefly batches events in memory to reduce syscall pressure at high RPM.
settings.streamFlushIntervalDesc: Minimum interval between flushes in coalesce mode, in milliseconds (1~1000).
settings.firstTokenModeDesc: Strict records only real content tokens (text / reasoning / tool arguments / images); Loose records the first response event after response.created / in_progress, so structural frames make first-token latency earlier.
settings.firstTokenExcludesWsAcquireDesc: When enabled, the first-token time recorded in usage logs excludes the WS connection acquire time (queueing/probing/handshake) of the request, reflecting only how fast the upstream produced the first content. Acquire time is still recorded separately in the Conn Acquire column; the two columns add up to the full duration. Off by default to keep the historical semantics. Only affects newly written logs.
settings.firstTokenTimeoutDesc: For streaming requests, cancel the current upstream call and retry with another account if the upstream returns no response event (other than response.created / in_progress) within N seconds; 0 = disabled. Structural and reasoning frames emitted during the thinking phase count as 'response started', so long reasoning turns are not interrupted by mistake.
settings.imageStorageDesc: Choose where generated images are persisted: local disk or any S3-compatible object store (AWS S3 / Cloudflare R2 / MinIO / Aliyun OSS / Tencent COS / B2, etc.).
settings.imageStorageBackendDesc: After switching to S3, new images go to the object store; existing local files remain readable.
settings.imageS3EndpointDesc: Service URL, e.g. https://{accountid}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com or https://oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com. Leave blank for AWS S3.
settings.imageS3RegionDesc: Region code; R2/MinIO can use auto.
settings.imageS3SecretKeyDesc: Secret key — stored in the database when saved.
settings.imageS3PrefixDesc: Optional; prepended to every object key, e.g. codex/images.
settings.imageS3ForcePathStyleDesc: Required by MinIO; usually off for AWS S3 / R2.
settings.backgroundImageDesc: Set a global admin background. Supports URLs, local paths, uploaded images, or MP4 live wallpapers; images can be up to 20MB, MP4 can be up to 40MB, and background/surface opacity and blur can be tuned separately.
settings.backgroundImageInvalidType: Background media must be PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG, or MP4
settings.backgroundImageTooLarge: Background image must be 20MB or smaller
settings.backgroundVideoTooLarge: MP4 live wallpaper must be 40MB or smaller

settings.autoResetCreditsDesc: Periodically checks Plus/Pro accounts and consumes one reset credit when the earliest credit is about to expire, preventing unused credits from expiring. Disabled by default.
settings.autoResetCreditsEnabledDesc: Runs once when enabled, then every 5 minutes. Each account consumes at most one credit per scan and records a reset_credit / auto audit event.
settings.autoResetCreditsBeforeExpiryDesc: Trigger when the earliest available credit expires within this window. Range: 10–10080 minutes; default: 60.
settings.globalAutoPauseDesc: Set default auto-pause thresholds for all accounts. Account-level or group-level settings take priority.
settings.autoPause5hGuardBandHint: Reduce concurrency when 5h usage nears the pause line to slow quota consumption. Enter how many percentage points early to start; 0 turns it off.
settings.autoPause5hGuardConcurrencyHint: When an account enters the 5h guard band, cap its concurrency at this value. Default is 1. Enter 0 to disable guard-band concurrency reduction.
settings.smartPacingEnabledHint: When enabled, if an account is burning quota faster than an even pace within a usage window, its concurrency is automatically scaled down to a sustainable rate so the remaining quota lasts until the window reset — avoiding hitting the 5h/7d limit early. Off by default.
settings.smartPacingWindowsHint: Which usage windows to pace on. When both are selected, the stricter result wins.
settings.smartPacingMinConcurrencyHint: Concurrency will not drop below this value while pacing, so an account is never fully starved. Default is 1.
settings.globalAutoPauseHint: Enter 0 to disable global default. Priority: Account > Group > Global.
settings.ignoreUsageLimitStatusHint: Allow only bound active turns carrying Codex turn state to continue when a usage window reports 100%. Fresh turns remain blocked, and /v1/responses usage_limit_reached stops continuation. Account overrides take priority.
settings.codexContinueThinkingDesc: When upstream truncates reasoning at the known fingerprint, silently resend with prior reasoning and fold rounds into one response. Each round is a real upstream request that multiplies quota usage, and this explicitly bypasses upstream truncation — use at your own risk. Disabled by default.
settings.codexContinueMaxRoundsDesc: Total upstream rounds allowed per request (including the first). Returns current result once reached. Range 1-32, default 8.
settings.utlsShutdownTimeoutDesc: Only applies when CODEX_TRANSPORT_MODE=utls_chrome. After a connection is evicted from the pool (GOAWAY received, connection error, or account recycled), this caps how long we wait for its in-flight requests to finish before forcing a close, so a hung stream can never pin the connection forever. Normal requests close immediately and never wait for this limit. Range 1-240, default 30 minutes.
settings.codexFingerprintDefaultMode: Default fingerprint mode for new accounts
settings.codexFingerprintDefaultModeDesc: Device fingerprint convergence level stamped on newly imported or newly added Codex accounts. Only affects accounts added afterwards — existing accounts keep their current level, and each account can still be adjusted individually after import. Only Codex accounts are affected; relay and Grok accounts ignore it. Default off.
settings.overflowAutoCompactDesc: When the upstream rejects a request with context_length_exceeded, the gateway summarizes older turns into a single context note and retries once instead of returning 400 to the client.
settings.overflowAutoCompactEnabledDesc: Experimental, off by default. Summarization runs an internal model call, consuming account quota and adding roughly 10s latency; the summary is lossy while recent turns are kept verbatim. Can also be enabled per key via limits.auto_compact_overflow.
settings.compactViaResponsesDesc: The official upstream removed the dedicated /responses/compact endpoint (now returns 404). When enabled, downstream /v1/responses/compact requests on official Codex OAuth accounts are rewritten as /responses calls with a compaction_trigger input item, and the streamed result is aggregated into a single JSON response.
settings.compactViaResponsesEnabledDesc: Off by default. Only affects compact passthrough on official OAuth accounts; relay (OpenAI Responses API) accounts still call their own /responses/compact endpoint.
settings.codexPreflightSSEPassthroughDesc: Forward pre-content upstream metadata events (codex.rate_limits / codex.response.metadata / response.metadata) to the downstream immediately instead of buffering them until the first real content event. For multi-tier gateways that treat the first SSE data frame as time-to-first-response.
settings.codexPreflightSSEPassthroughEnabledDesc: Warning: legacy compatibility mode, off by default. When enabled, HTTP 200 is committed before the first content event; upstream failures in that window can only be delivered as 200 + SSE failed frames — real HTTP error codes, pre-first-token silent account rotation, and overflow auto-compact are all unavailable in that window. Hot-reloads without restart.
settings.modelCooldownDesc: Control model-level 429 cooldowns separately for direct API upstreams and OAuth account pools. Explicit 5h/7d usage windows still follow their real reset times.
settings.relayModelCooldownDesc: Persistent model cooldown is off by default. Transient 429s rotate upstreams and return a standard 429 only after retries are exhausted.
settings.oauthModelCooldownDesc: Keep account-pool protection while allowing cooldowns to be disabled, fixed, or adaptive.
settings.modelCooldownModeDesc: Off stores no model cooldown; fixed uses a constant duration; adaptive can back off on repeated 429s.
settings.modelCooldownSecondsDesc: Base model cooldown duration from 1 to 1800 seconds.
settings.modelCooldownBackoffDesc: Adaptive mode only. Repeated 429s extend the cooldown up to 30 minutes.

proxies.description: Manage the proxy pool. Unbound accounts stick to an enabled proxy; binding pins an account to one egress. Disabling stops use immediately, deleting unbinds, and direct egress is refused while the pool is on.
proxies.addFirstProxy: Please add at least one proxy first
proxies.poolFailClosedHint: While on, requests and token refresh use a proxy. A disabled pin keeps the account off that egress until re-enabled instead of going direct. Unbound accounts only use still-enabled proxies.
proxies.cleanErrorDesc: This will permanently delete all {{count}} error proxies and remove their account bindings. This cannot be undone.
proxies.cleanErrorSuccess: Cleared {{count}} error proxies and unbound {{unbound}} accounts
proxies.addProxyDesc: One proxy URL per line, supports http:// / https:// / socks5:// format
proxies.noProxiesDesc: Click "Add Proxy" to configure the proxy pool
proxies.bindHint: Binding writes this proxy into the account's proxy_url so that account always uses it. Binding is not exclusive: unbound accounts can still be assigned the same enabled proxy from the pool. Disabling keeps the pin but stops using that egress immediately; deleting clears the pin. Unbound accounts fail over inside the enabled pool, and never go direct while the pool is on.

proxies.balanceDesc: Distribute refreshable OAuth accounts evenly across enabled, reachable proxies (least-bound first). API-key, relay API, and access-token-only accounts are excluded from auto-assignment, and their existing manual bindings stay unchanged.
proxies.balanceModeUnboundHint: Manually bound OAuth accounts stay untouched; only unbound OAuth accounts get assigned.
proxies.balanceModeAllHint: All OAuth accounts participate: valid bindings under the cap are kept and the rest are reassigned; non-OAuth accounts stay unchanged.

Other tools (shell, function, apply_patch, MCP, web search) are kept. Use this when the upstream group/plan does not support image generation but should still serve text and code.
imageGenerationPolicyHint.block: Requests that touch image generation (gpt-image-* models, /v1/images endpoints, or an image_generation tool/intent) return 403.

limits.dailyHint: Daily limits follow the server's calendar day and fully reset at midnight; 5h/7d/30d are rolling windows where usage gradually ages out.

limits.scopeGroupMissing: This group no longer exists; saving will be rejected.
limits.scopeQuotaResetDesc: Zero out the amount already used on this group/account. Cumulative budgets never decay on their own, so the budget becomes usable again right after the reset.

guide.description: Learn how to configure and call CodexProxy API endpoints

guide.responsesDesc: Native Codex Responses API endpoint. Directly proxies requests to upstream. For Codex CLI, OpenAI SDK and other native clients.
guide.chatDesc: OpenAI Chat Completions compatible endpoint. Accepts OpenAI format, translates to Codex format, and translates responses back. For ChatGPT compatible clients.
guide.messagesDesc: Anthropic Messages API compatible endpoint. Accepts Claude format, translates to Codex format, and translates responses back. For Claude Code and other Anthropic clients.
guide.codexDesc: Add the following configuration files to the Codex CLI config directory to use Codex models through this proxy.
guide.codexConfigHint: Make sure the following content is at the beginning of config.toml
guide.codexNoteUnix: Make sure the config directory exists. Run mkdir -p ~/.codex to create it.
guide.codexNoteWindows: Press Win+R, type %userprofile%\.codex to open the config directory. Create it manually if it doesn't exist.
guide.claudeCodeDesc: Set environment variables or edit settings.json to let Claude Code use Codex models through this proxy.
guide.claudeCodeNote: Replace YOUR_API_KEY with the API Key created on the API Keys page. Model mapping can be configured in Settings.
guide.claudeEnvNote: These environment variables only apply to the current terminal session. For permanent configuration, add them to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc.
guide.claudeSettingsNote: Or directly edit the Claude Code settings.json config file (choose one method).
guide.authDesc: All endpoints support the following authentication methods (in priority order):
guide.modelMappingDesc: Model mapping is split into Claude mapping and Codex model redirects. Codex mapping supports * wildcard rules such as gpt-*, *-mini, or *codex*.
