docs.title: Payload Rewrite Guide
docs.description: How to rewrite upstream JSON request bodies before they reach the model: system prompts, service_tier, reasoning effort, and arbitrary field paths.

what.title: What this module does
what.p1: Payload rewrite mutates the client JSON body after it hits the gateway and before it is sent upstream. Typical uses include appending or replacing instructions, forcing service_tier, and remapping reasoning.effort.
what.p2: Rules apply immediately after save. The gateway has no default system prompt of its own—instructions are client-provided, and rules layer on top of that pass-through.
what.b1: Visual editor with templates, plus a full JSON source mode.
what.b2: Rule groups control write semantics: set-if-missing, override, string append, or field removal.
what.b3: Match gates filter by model, headers, field presence, and field values.
what.b4: Observed samples show pre-rewrite client instructions for reference.

pipeline.title: Request pipeline
pipeline.p1: A request roughly flows through the engine as follows:
pipeline.s1: Parse the client body (chat/responses-style endpoints; image generation is not affected).
pipeline.s2: Select rules that pass their group configuration and match gates.
pipeline.s3: Apply writes using default / override / append / filter (and raw variants).
pipeline.s4: Skip protected fields so routing and streaming stay intact.
pipeline.s5: Forward the rewritten body upstream; optionally record original instructions samples.

groups.title: Choosing a rule group
groups.p1: Each rule belongs to a group that defines how fields are written.
groups.default: Write only when the field is missing; never overwrite client values.
groups.override: Always set the target value, replacing any existing one.
groups.append: Concatenate onto string fields (e.g. append text to instructions).
groups.raw: Raw variants parse the value as JSON before writing—useful for nested objects.
groups.callout: Overriding instructions replaces the official Codex CLI system prompt and may affect tool calling. It also invalidates upstream prompt cache—keep rule text stable.

gates.title: Match gates
gates.p1: A rule runs only when every configured gate matches. Empty means unrestricted.
gates.b1: models: names or wildcards (e.g. gpt-*); empty = all models.
gates.b2: headers: require specific request header values.
gates.b3: match / not_match: body field paths equal / not equal given values.
gates.b4: exist / not_exist: field paths must be present / absent.
gates.b5: Multiple gates combine with AND semantics.

identity.title: Identity gates (Key / group)
identity.p1: Beyond matching on body content, rules can be scoped by the downstream identity behind the request: the downstream API Key and the account groups it may use. Great for per-customer or per-plan rewrites.
identity.p2: Values within a single gate are OR'd (any match passes); these gates combine with models / headers / match gates via AND, so all must pass for the rule to run. All values support wildcard * and are case-insensitive.
identity.b1: api_key_ids: downstream API Key IDs (as strings), wildcard supported.
identity.b2: api_key_names: downstream API Key names, wildcard supported.
identity.b3: group_ids: account-group IDs (as strings) the Key may use, wildcard supported.
identity.b5: Empty = unrestricted. If a rule sets any identity gate but the request has no resolvable identity, the rule does not match (fail-closed).
identity.callout: Identity gates only apply on Codex endpoints (/v1/responses, /v1/messages, /v1/chat/completions), NOT on compact / relay channels. The Fast Group Boost template is built on the group gate.

templates.title: Built-in templates
templates.p1: When adding a rule, start from a template and refine as needed.
templates.b1: Append system prompt: keep the original text and append yours.
templates.b2: Override system prompt: replace instructions entirely.
templates.b3: Override service_tier: force a tier such as priority.
templates.b4: Reasoning effort mapping: e.g. lift medium to high.
templates.b6: Fast Group Boost: force service_tier for a chosen account group.
templates.b5: Custom rule: set/override/append/remove any path with full gates.
templates.callout: If you are unsure what clients send, inspect Observed samples first, then choose append vs override.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.p1: Prefer a low-risk append rule first, then add conditions and overrides.
quickstart.s1: Open Rules, click Add Rule, pick Append System Prompt.
quickstart.s2: Enter the text to append; optionally limit target models.
quickstart.s3: Save and send a couple of real client requests to verify.
quickstart.s4: Compare Observed samples with expected rewrite behavior.
quickstart.s5: Add tier/effort mappings or custom field rules as needed.

protected.title: Protected fields
protected.p1: These fields cannot be rewritten, so scheduling and protocol stay safe:
protected.b2: Rewrite business fields instead (instructions, service_tier, reasoning.effort, text.verbosity, …).
protected.b3: Use dotted paths for nested fields, e.g. reasoning.effort.
protected.callout: If a rule seems ignored, check protected fields, overly strict gates, and whether you clicked Save.

samples.title: Using observed samples
samples.p1: The bottom of the editor lists recently captured client instructions (before rewrite).
samples.b1: Compare against official/client system prompts before overriding.
samples.b2: Copy snippets into your append text.
samples.b3: If empty, wait for real traffic through the gateway.

json.title: JSON source mode
json.p1: Visual and JSON modes convert both ways. Shape is { group: [rule objects…] }.
json.p2: Invalid JSON or structure blocks switching back to visual until fixed.
json.b1: Rule fields: models, headers, match, not_match, exist, not_exist, params.
json.b2: For filter, params is an array of paths; for other groups, params is a path→value object.
json.b3: After save, the server uses the new rules immediately—no restart.

checklist.title: Go-live checklist
checklist.s1: Choose append vs override deliberately and assess Codex tool-calling impact.
checklist.s2: Scope non-global rules with models or match gates.
checklist.s4: Regression-test with observed samples and real clients.
checklist.s5: Confirm Save succeeded; optionally audit the JSON source.
